terra.problem: The list does not keep rolling past Sarai. The text specifically mentions her, then moves on to Terah’s journey.
‘Nobody got left in Ur’ goes beyond the text. It names the people Terah took but does not say nobody was left behind.
The place and Terah’s son share a name, but the text does not say the family loved reusing names or named the place.
Nineveh being a city is a Bible fact from outside this passage and needs a reference.
The line about Terah having earned a rest makes light of his death rather than treating the heavy moment with care.
The joke mentions snacks. Cookies are the only food allowed in jokes and comparisons.
Checking an oven timer does not connect clearly to the action in the promise. The joke does not pass the comparison logic test.
Leaving his father’s household does not mean that household is excluded from the promised blessing. The promise reaches all the families of the earth.
The text says the Canaanites were in the land, not that they were living around Abram at the Oak of Moreh.
The text does not say Abram had no city plan. It also mentions his tent later, not that he was traveling with tents.
The text places the tent and altar in the hill country but does not say the altar was right beside the tent.
